questions.question: What is an algorithm in the context of social media?
options: A set of rules deciding what content you see online
A type of computer screen
A social media influencer
A maths exam task
questions.explanation: Algorithms are sets of rules that decide what appears in your feed, based on data about what you watch, like and share.

questions.question: What is the "digital divide"?
options: Inequality in access to technology between groups or countries
The line between two halves of a screen
A disagreement between tech companies
The gap between two software updates
questions.explanation: The digital divide refers to unequal access to technology and the internet, which creates disadvantages for some groups and countries.

questions.question: What does "bias in AI" mean?
options: When algorithms discriminate because they were trained on skewed data
When a robot physically leans to one side
When AI works perfectly for everyone
When computers run slowly
questions.explanation: AI systems trained on biased data can discriminate - for example, facial recognition that works worse for certain groups.

questions.question: Which is a real ethical dilemma connected to automation?
options: Machines replacing human jobs and what happens to those workers
Robots demanding holidays
Computers becoming bored at work
Phones refusing to charge
questions.explanation: Automation raises the dilemma of efficiency versus employment: machines can replace human jobs, affecting people's livelihoods.

questions.question: What is the dilemma of "privacy vs. security"?
options: Surveillance can increase safety but reduces people's right to a private life
Passwords are hard to remember
Privacy and security are the same thing
Security cameras are too expensive
questions.explanation: More surveillance may prevent crime but means collecting data about innocent people, threatening the right to privacy.
